title: Vietnam news agency says sorry for false report on prosecutions
text: Vietnam's state-run news agency apologized on Saturday for publishing what it described as a false report that two more officials of state energy company PetroVietnam would be prosecuted over financial losses. The original report had also appeared on the government's official website. In a statement, Vietnam News Agency said it had apologized to Phung Dinh Thuc and Do Van Hau over the false report, as well as to their families and to police. The agency said it had not checked its information carefully enough before publishing it. PetroVietnam is at the center of a sweeping high-level crackdown on corruption in the communist state. Former PetroVietnam chairman Dinh La Thang, 56, was arrested on Friday. A former member of Vietnam's politburo, he is the most senior executive to be arrested so far. Thang's brother, Dinh Manh Thang, a former chairman of a PetroVietnam unit, was also arrested over allegations that he violated state regulations on economic management. Critics of the government have voiced suspicions that the crackdown is at least partly politically motivated and targeted at people close to former Prime Minister Nguyen Tan Dung, who lost an internal power struggle in 2016. The crackdown made headlines around the world in August, when Germany accused Vietnam of kidnapping former executive Trinh Xuan Thanh in Berlin to bring him to trial over a separate case.

White, now a senior fellow at the Texas Public Policy Institute, has questioned the idea that burning fossil fuels is causing harmful increases in global temperatures. title: Conflicting Stories Emerge After Police Action At Treaty Camp
text: More details are coming out about yesterday's police action on Highway 1806, about three miles from the Cannonball River. Starting shortly before noon, a large contingent of heavily armed officers worked to clear a path for Dakota Access oil pipeline (DAPL) trenches in a relentless push that led to numerous violent confrontations and ended with the seizure of the newly established Treaty Camp and the removal of a number of tents, tipis and sweat lodges. The Morton County Sheriff's Department said 141 people had been arrested and that at least one bullet had been fired from the frontlines. “Officers met violence and resistance including a protester who fired a gun at officers in the police line, protesters who threw molotov cocktails at them and set vehicles and debris on fire,” the sheriff's office said in a post on Facebook. A news story by the Associated Press cites state spokesperson Cecily Wong describing a woman who drew a .38 caliber pistol and fired three times at officers, an account that activists dispute and that does not appear on any of the on-the-scene video or live feeds now circulating. Tribal law enforcement, however, apprehended a heavily armed man crouching in a creek with apparent connections to a private security firm hired by DAPL's builders. The Standing Rock Sioux Tribe posted a description of the incident on its Facebook page. According to the tribe, a man was apprehended carrying an assault rifle, with papers indicating that he was employed by a private security firm. “As reported via video evidence from the front lines on 10-27-16. A man bearing an assault rifle broke thru a barricade and was speeding toward the Oceti Sakowin camp, he was run off the road 1/4 mile north from the Camp.”

title: Rasmussen: 57 Percent Back a Temporary Ban on Refugees From Terror-Exporting Countries
text: A strong majority of voters back a temporary ban on refugees from unstable and violent countries, Rasmussen Reports has found. title: Suez says it has temporarily moved Catalonia office to Madrid
text: France's Suez, Spain's leading water provider, has temporarily shifted the legal registration of its offices in Catalonia to Madrid because of legal uncertainty linked to Catalonia's independence movement. Suez sells water to municipal and industrial customers in Spain, where last year it generated 2.5 billion euros of its 15.3 billion euros in total revenue. "We have temporarily moved the registered office of Agbar, which is the (Suez) holding company in Catalonia, to Madrid in order to protect the legal certainty of investors, because what we see now in Catalonia is uncertainty," Chief Financial Officer Christophe Cros said on an earnings call. He said Suez had already moved the legal address of the holding company that owns all its activities in Spain from Barcelona to Madrid in 2015. That move was not about politics, he said, but because the company wanted a stronger presence in Madrid, as Catalonia accounts for only about 50 percent of Suez's revenue in Spain. Cros said business in Spain as a whole, as well as in Catalonia, had been good in the first nine months of the year. "Our business in Catalonia is to deliver water to consumers and I don't expect any change in the need in water," he said. In 2015, when Suez completed its full takeover of Aguas de Barcelona (Agbar), former Agbar minority shareholder Criteria Caixa became Suez's second-largest shareholder, and it now holds 5.74 percent of its shares. Suez's Spanish water unit Agbar, whose roots go back to 1882, has over 12,600 staff worldwide and generated 60 percent of its revenue in Spain, with the rest coming mainly from Chile.

title: Miracles Man: Metaxas Takes On Closed Minds And A Closed Universe
text: Last Christmas, Christian apologist Eric Metaxas wrote an article for the opinion section of the Wall Street Journal about a ‘miracle’, or perhaps I should say ‘the miracle’: the origin of the universe. That article, Science Increasingly Makes the Case for God, went on to become, if not quite a miracle, at least a kind of wonder. It was shared by email and on social media more than any other opinion article in the Wall Street Journal's history. That is really saying something, since the Journal is known for having one of the most popular op/ed pages in the world. Former editor Robert Bartley once quipped that his was the only opinion page in journalism that actually sold papers. Metaxas clearly tapped into something. As of this writing this morning, the article has more than 470,000 Facebook shares and well over 9,000 comments. The wonder is not the article itself but the phenomenon that, in an age of angry pop atheism and sloppy ‘God-is-dead’ science journalism, intelligent, well-educated people, the sort who read the Wall Street Journal, still have minds open to the idea that the universe is not closed; that there is something (or Someone) beyond it who can intervene in it, Who set it whirling into existence in the first place. I recently sat down with Metaxas over a Skype line to talk about the paperback release of his book, Miracles: What They Are, Why They Happen, and How They Can Change Your Life. The first third of the book deals with philosophical questions: Are miracles possible? What exactly are they? And why are philosophical objections to them not quite as final or decisive as they claim to be?

title: Ex-chief of Chinese news agency expelled from party over graft
text: The retired former head of a Chinese state-run news agency has been thrown out of the ruling Communist Party for graft, an anti-corruption watchdog said on Monday. Liu Beixian, who was editor-in-chief of the China News Service until he retired in February 2015, took bribes and expensive gifts and abused his power to secure financial gain for private companies, the watchdog, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, said in a statement. The commission said Liu, 62, had also broken regulations by flying first class several times and had been uncooperative during the investigation. "As a leading cadre, Liu Beixian lost his ideals and convictions and had serious thoughts of privilege," the commission said, adding that the evidence would be handed to the relevant judicial authorities for prosecution. Liu or a legal or family representative could not be reached for comment. Liu was placed under investigation in August for "serious disciplinary violations", a euphemism for graft. The China News Service operates under the auspices of the cabinet's Overseas Chinese Affairs Office and is meant to serve as a news source for Chinese communities in places such as Hong Kong and self-ruled Taiwan. It is separate from Xinhua, China's official news agency. According to his official resume, Liu started working at the China News Service in 1983 and was its Hong Kong bureau chief from 1997 to 2000. The former British territory was returned to China in 1997. Since taking office five years ago, President Xi Jinping has waged a sweeping campaign against deep-rooted corruption, jailing or handing lesser punishments to hundreds of thousands of officials.

title: Palestinians tell Trump they remain committed to two-state solution
text: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Wednesday called for a halt to Israeli settlement expansion in occupied territory and said he remained committed to a two-state solution to the conflict with Israel, after U.S. President Donald Trump suggested he might be open to alternatives. Abbas's office released a statement after Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a news conference in Washington ahead of a meeting. At the news conference, Trump told Netanyahu: “I’d like to see you pull back on settlements for a little bit.” But Trump also abandoned U.S. insistence on a two-state solution, a longstanding bedrock of Middle East policy, overturning a position embraced by successive administrations and the international community as well as a U.S. commitment to the eventual creation of a Palestinian state. Abbas said he agreed with Trump's call for Israel to hold back on settlement building in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem. “The presidency demands that (Israel) agree to (Trump’s call), and that of the international community, to halt all settlement activities including in occupied East Jerusalem,” the statement said. But the Palestinians emphasized that they wanted the two-state option. “The Palestinian presidency stressed its commitment to the two-state solution and to the international law and international legitimacy in the way that secures ending the Israeli occupation and establish the Palestinian State with East Jerusalem as its capital.” Asked whether he supported a two-state solution, Trump gave a convoluted answer, suggesting he could go along with whatever the two sides decided. “I’m looking at two states and one state, and I like the one both parties like,” he said, standing beside Netanyahu. “I can live with either one.”
